title: The Muscle Cuff Regenerative Peripheral Nerve Interface for the Amplification of Intact Peripheral Nerve Signals
protocol: Anesthetize the experimental rat utilizing a solution of 5% isoflurane in oxygen at 0.8-1.0 L/min in an induction chamber.
Place the rat on a rebreather nose cone with isoflurane lowered to 1.75%-2.25% for maintenance of anesthesia once adequate anesthesia is achieved and confirmed with the absence of corneal reflex.
Inject a solution of 0.02-0.03 mL Carprofen (50 mg/mL) in 0.2 mL of sterile saline with 27 G needle in the subcutaneous plane between the shoulder blades for peri- and post-operative analgesia.
Apply sterile eye ointment to both eyes to prevent corneal ulcers while anesthetized.
Shave the lateral portion of the bilateral lower limbs extending from the hip joint, over the thigh, and to the dorsal surface of the paw using an electric razor.
Sterilize the surgical site by wiping with an alcohol prep pad.
Apply povidone-iodine solution to the surgical site.
Cleanse the area again with a new alcohol prep pad to remove residual povidone-iodine solution.
Repeat the alternating cleansing process three times to maintain sterility.
Place the rat on a heating pad underneath a surgical microscope for body temperature monitoring using an intraoral probe.
Maintain isoflurane at 1.75%-2.25% and oxygen at 0.8-1.0 L/min during surgery.
Make a longitudinal incision along the anterior aspect of the desired donor hindlimb extending from just above the ankle to just below the knee with a #15 scalpel.
Dissect through the underlying subcutaneous tissue using sharp iris scissors to expose the tibialis anterior and extensor digitorum longus muscles.
Isolate the EDL muscle and its distal tendon from the surrounding musculature.
Ensure isolation of the correct tendon by inserting both tines of a forceps or iris scissor underneath the distal tendon just proximal to the ankle joint.
Exert upward pressure on the tendon by opening either the forceps or iris scissors.
Perform a distal tenotomy of the EDL muscle at the level of the ankle with sharp iris scissors.
Dissect the muscle free from surrounding tissues working proximally towards its tendinous origin.
Once the proximal tendon is visualized, perform a proximal tenotomy utilizing sharp iris scissors to free the graft.
Trim both tendinous ends of the muscle graft and cut to the desired length with sharp iris scissors.
On one side of the muscle graft, make a longitudinal incision along the entire trimmed length.
Place the prepared muscle graft in a saline-moistened gauze to prevent tissue desiccation.
Close the skin overlying the donor site with 4-0 chromic suture in a running fashion.
Mark the surgical incision from a line ~5 mm from the sciatic notch extending to just inferior to the knee joint.
Incise through the skin and subcutaneous tissues along the marked incision line with a #15 blade.
Carefully incise through the underlying biceps femoris fascia without extending through the entire depth of the muscle.
Dissect carefully through the biceps femoris muscle using blunt-tipped small scissors or a hemostat.
Identify the common peroneal (CP) nerve.
Carefully isolate the CP nerve from surrounding nerves using micro-forceps and micro-scissors.
Remove any surrounding connective tissue from the middle 2 cm of the CP nerve.
Perform an epineurial window over the central-most portion of the freed CP nerve.
Hold the proximal epineurium with micro-forceps.
Cut into the epineurium immediately underlying with micro-dissection scissors.
Remove approximately 25% of the epineurium traveling distally along the nerve in one piece.
Ensure that the nerve tissue underlying the epineurium has a goo-like texture to confirm correct removal.
Place the muscle graft from the saline-moistened gauze under the central portion of the CP nerve where the epineurial window was created.
Rotate the nerve 180° so the epineurial window section contacts intact muscle and does not underlie the eventual suture line.
Suture the epineurium of the CP nerve both proximally and distally to the muscle graft using 8-0 nylon sutures.
Secure the muscle graft to the endomysium with simple interrupted stitches.
Wrap the edges of the muscle graft circumferentially and suture in place with simple interrupted 8-0 nylon stitches.
Close the biceps femoris fascia over the construct using 5-0 chromic suture in a running fashion.
Close the overlying skin using a 4-0 chromic suture in a running fashion.
Cleans the surgical area with an alcohol prep pad.
Apply antibiotic ointment to the surgical site.
Terminate inhalational anesthesia.
Place the rat in a clean cage isolated from cage mates and allow recovery with food and water ad libitum.
